**🚀 Performance & Scalability** | **🔵 Trivial** | **🏗️ Heavy lift**

**Memoize the syntax-backed receiver check for each test.**

`inherent_receiver_call_resolves` parses the complete `test.body` each time it is called (`parse_clean_source_file(&test.body)`). After the parse, it walks all descendants. For each supported assertion macro, it also formats and parses one synthetic source file per operand.

In the compact path, `match_direct_owner_call` calls this function inside the loop over `tests_by_call_name[owner.name]`. That loop runs once per seam. Before this change, the receiver check ran only when `same_name_count > 1`. It now runs for every parser-established inherent `&self` owner. The parse work therefore grows as seams × tests that call the name. Several seams can share one owner: the new fixture alone has four `as_object` seams.

The masked-text precheck filters some calls. It does not filter tests whose receiver the old nominal matcher already resolves. With common inherent method names such as `len`, `get`, `is_empty` or `as_str`, many test bodies are parsed repeatedly. The comment at `OwnerContext::resolve` (`#7716`) already records that the codebase shares per-test parses across seams for this reason.

Cache the result per test, keyed by `(method, impl_type)`. Alternatively, cache the parsed `SyntaxNode` per test, for example in a `OnceLock` on `CompactTest`, or in a per-run memo like `shared_owner_call_identity`. Then every seam and every probe reuses one parse.

🔴 **Foreign helper falsely reaches private owner** When `read_as_object()` calls only a foreign receiver's `as_object`, the helper graph still credits the private inherent owner. `helper_name_carries_owner_token` accepts the name without checking that helper call's receiver. Repository reach evidence then attributes an unrelated test to the owner.
Learn more A helper-to-owner edge is a claim that running a test helper executes the production owner. The new same-name guard excludes the helper's own declaration but leaves other helper names eligible through [helper_name_carries_owner_token](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/15ca898ad1d3571d104ce1ae20b629fe2f55fc86/crates/ripr/src/analysis/test_grip_evidence/related_tests/context.rs "crates/ripr/src/analysis/test_grip_evidence/related_tests/context.rs") and a textual call check. [match_helper_owner_call](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/15ca898ad1d3571d104ce1ae20b629fe2f55fc86/crates/ripr/src/analysis/test_grip_evidence/related_tests.rs#L300-L330 "crates/ripr/src/analysis/test_grip_evidence/related_tests.rs:300-330") then grants reach without calling the new receiver validator. This permits the wrong receiver to bypass the direct-call refusal. **Example:** An inherent `JsonValue::as_object` exists. A test calls `read_as_object()`, whose body returns `serde_json::json!({}).as_object()`. The test does not run `JsonValue::as_object`, but the helper edge can mark its seam reached. **Recommended fix:** Apply bounded receiver attribution to the actual helper call sites when building inherent-method helper edges, or withhold those edges when the last-hop receiver cannot be established. Add a negative helper fixture alongside the genuine-helper positive control and check full and compact evidence.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔴 **Shadowed assertion macro falsely credits owner** When a module-level `assert_eq!` ignores its arguments, `inherent_assertion_arguments_resolve` still treats their calls as executed. The shadow check inspects `StmtList` but not module item lists. A test can receive direct-owner credit without running the owner.
Learn more Standard assertion macros evaluate their expression operands, but a user-defined macro of the same name can discard them. The check visits block statement lists while `macro_rules!` defined in an enclosing module lives in that module's item list. The token-tree parser then treats the discarded expression as a real method call, and [owner_call_relation_reason](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/15ca898ad1d3571d104ce1ae20b629fe2f55fc86/crates/ripr/src/analysis/classify/related_tests.rs#L3438-L3445 "crates/ripr/src/analysis/classify/related_tests.rs:3438-3445") can promote the relation. **Example:** In `mod tests`, define `macro_rules! assert_eq { ($($tokens:tt)*) => {} }`. A test binds `let value = JsonValue::Null` and writes `assert_eq!(value.as_object(), None)`. The expansion runs no call, but the test receives direct-owner credit. **Recommended fix:** Resolve or conservatively reject same-named macro definitions and imports from the test's enclosing module scopes before interpreting an assertion token tree. Pin an ignoring module-level macro as a negative production-path control.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Expired sibling shadow hides real calls** After an inner block shadows `value`, `inherent_receiver_call_resolves` can reject a genuine later `value.as_object()` call. The text prefilter reads the expired inner `let`, so the scope-aware matcher never runs. Genuine owner tests lose direct-call credit.
Learn more The prefilter uses [last_let_statement](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/15ca898ad1d3571d104ce1ae20b629fe2f55fc86/crates/ripr/src/analysis/classify/related_tests.rs#L2421 "crates/ripr/src/analysis/classify/related_tests.rs:2421") on text preceding a call. That scan does not distinguish live declarations from declarations in a closed block. The subsequent AST walk knows lexical scope, but cannot restore a candidate already rejected by this early return. Both diff and compact relationship consumers invoke this helper. **Example:** `let value = JsonValue::Null; { let value = serde_json::Value::Null; } assert!(value.as_object().is_none());` calls the outer `JsonValue` method. The prefilter sees the inner `serde_json` binding last and rejects it. **Recommended fix:** Avoid using the scope-unaware text matcher as a deny gate for parser-confirmed calls; let the AST evaluate candidate calls directly. Add a sibling-block shadow positive control to both relationship surfaces.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Same-named wrappers lose genuine reach** When `Wrapper::as_object` forwards to `JsonValue::as_object`, the self-name filter removes its real delegation. Tests calling the wrapper cannot pass [match_direct_owner_call](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/15ca898ad1d3571d104ce1ae20b629fe2f55fc86/crates/ripr/src/analysis/test_grip_evidence/related_tests.rs#L257-L278 "crates/ripr/src/analysis/test_grip_evidence/related_tests.rs:257-278") either. Repository evidence misses their genuine route to the owner.
Learn more The call-fact list includes the function declaration's name, which motivated removing a spurious self edge. It also includes actual calls from the body. Filtering every fact named like the containing function removes real calls when one method wraps another method with the same name. [match_direct_owner_call](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/15ca898ad1d3571d104ce1ae20b629fe2f55fc86/crates/ripr/src/analysis/test_grip_evidence/related_tests.rs#L257-L278 "crates/ripr/src/analysis/test_grip_evidence/related_tests.rs:257-278") cannot compensate when the test calls only the wrapper. **Example:** `Wrapper::as_object` returns `self.inner.as_object()` with `inner: JsonValue`. A test calls `wrapper.as_object()`, which runs the private owner, but no helper edge is recorded for it. **Recommended fix:** Distinguish declaration call facts from executable body calls rather than excluding an entire name. Preserve same-name delegations when the forwarded receiver is established, and test a wrapper sharing its owner's method name.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

**Reuse one `OwnerPinSyntax` for the analysis run.**

`inherent_receiver_call_resolves` creates a fresh `OwnerPinSyntax` for every invocation. Calls that reach targeted macro binding or unit-struct resolution then repeat the workspace scans that `OwnerPinSyntax` is designed to memoize. The full classifier and compact `tests_by_call_name` path can invoke this repeatedly across owner/test matches. Helper traversal can also repeat it for each checked hop. The existing parsed-body work does not cache these scans.

Pass a shared run-scoped `OwnerPinSyntax` from the owning analysis context. The assertion and binding gates mean that not every assertion macro reaches both scans, but the reachable repeated workspace work remains material for large workspaces.

**[P1] Repository direct calls bypass the existing module-type shadow refusal**

Verified current and inherited on exact parent43. With root `JsonValue::as_object` and a distinct `tests::JsonValue::as_object`, the test calls only its module-local type. Diff correctly retains weak/low; this repository route calls only the syntax receiver checker and gives the root owner direct/high, making all four owner seams strongly_gripped. Fresh compact output agrees. The native test passes both original and root-owner mutant; a paired genuine-owner test kills the mutant.

The helper last-hop route already uses `inherent_owner_call_resolves`, which includes the source/module shadow refusal. Reuse that complete authority here rather than bypassing it. Add this module-shadow case to the full/compact/diff honesty controls; no general type resolver is needed.

[Complete minimal sources, native results and raw consumer reports](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/tree/28b14701b8c0d773db61081f2fde3ce963b009cb/evidence/8004/independent-review53/controls/module-direct-shadow); paired positive is `module-owner-positive`. Confidence: high, executable counterexample.

**[P1] Uncalled nested function bodies supply direct-owner credit**

Verified current and inherited on exact parent43. A test only defines `fn dormant() { let value = JsonValue::Object(7); assert_eq!(value.as_object(), Some(7)); }` and then asserts `7 == 7`. Both descendant sweeps enter the dormant function. Diff emits direct/high and full/fresh compact repository output strongly grips all four owner seams, although the test never executes the owner. Native original and owner-mutant tests both pass; adding an actual `dormant()` invocation makes the mutant fail.

Exclude nested item/function bodies from the outer test's executable syntax. If nested-helper execution is admitted, require an actual resolved call; otherwise withhold credit. This is declaration-versus-execution, not arbitrary value-flow inference.

[Minimal source and raw reports](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/tree/28b14701b8c0d773db61081f2fde3ce963b009cb/evidence/8004/independent-review53/controls/dormant-nested); native negative and invoked positive are retained in `native/dormant-nested` and `native/nested-invoked`. Confidence: high.

**[P1] Explicit foreign free-helper entry borrows a same-named root helper**

Verified current and inherited on exact parent43. Root `read_as_object()` genuinely calls the owner, while sibling `foreign::read_as_object()` only returns `Some(7)`. A test calling exclusively the explicit foreign path passes this name/spelling predicate for the unrelated root helper. Full repository output grants helper/high and strongly grips all four owner seams; fresh compact output agrees. The native test survives the owner mutation, while changing it to call the root helper kills that mutation.

Bind the free-helper entry to the actual module/function declaration, or withhold ambiguous entry; apply that rule at intermediate hops too. A helper-name graph is candidate evidence, not function identity. Preserve the unique genuine-helper positive.

[Complete minimal sources and raw reports](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/tree/28b14701b8c0d773db61081f2fde3ce963b009cb/evidence/8004/independent-review53/controls/sibling-helper); native paired root-helper positive is `sibling-helper-positive`. Confidence: high.

[P1, source-derived; native/CLI confirmation blocked by environment provisioning] Assertion operand parsing omits the async exclusion used by the outer executable walk. `assert_eq!({ let _ = async { JsonValue::Object(7).as_object() }; 7 }, 7)` passes this operand's refusal scan (wildcard lets allowed), then its dormant method call reaches `resolves`. The future is never polled. Apply executable-body filtering here as well and retain paired native/full/compact/diff controls, including a genuine outer call. The existing dormant-async matrix case places async outside the assertion and does not exercise this route.

**[P1] Refuse execution credit from an unpolled async-function helper**

Failure mode: with the existing `JsonValue::as_object` owner, define:
```rust
async fn read_as_object() -> Option<u32> {
    JsonValue::Object(7).as_object()
}
```
and test `assert_eq!({ let _ = super::read_as_object(); 7 }, 7)`. This only constructs and discards a future. Native original and owner-mutant both pass, but the exact-a2 full CLI gives all four owner seams `helper_owner_call/high` and `strongly_gripped`. Fresh compact grip counts agree. A supported-name async intermediate hop reproduces it on source and the frozen-main composition.

Why here: resolving the actual declaration does not establish execution of an async body. This call view walks the helper's outer function; `node_executes_in` excludes descendant async blocks while exempting that outer async function.

Fix direction: conservatively refuse parsed async helper bodies at entry/intermediate/last-hop admission unless supported activation is established. Reuse existing syntax authority; no general polling, macro or type/value-flow expansion is needed.

Validation: add these native/full/fresh-compact/diff negatives and honesty-corpus controls while preserving the 34 existing cases and genuine synchronous/mixed positives. [Complete minimal source, raw reports and native logs](https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/tree/b78adbd0ce0dfd5f0baf438497b292133e1c1dc0/evidence/8004/independent-a2-review/findings/async-function-operand).

Confidence: high; executed current source and composition counterexamples.

**📐 Maintainability & Code Quality** | **🔵 Trivial** | **⚡ Quick win**
